title: QA: the Ophan of Hours in the sky
eyebrow: QA for pull request 445, issue #418 (steps #439 to #444) · merged into staging, not main · manual co-op test still owed
approval: QA passed: the Ophan in the sky

unverified: Nobody has played it by hand yet: every check was run by a script (manual co-op test still owed).
The drone and screen shake have not been listened to or felt by a person.
The slow beam seen from a third player's spot reads as a short, wide shard near the eye; whether that looks right is your call.
The clips are slowed down and taken frame by frame (about 6 frames a second of playback), so they show what happens, not how smooth it looks at full speed.

short.lead: In the last minute of a raid the Ophan of Hours hangs in the sky with its wings spread, watches whoever carries the most, locks on, and drains them with a beam unless stone is between you. Hide too long and it charges a beam that goes through stone, kills, and scorches the room open. Carry an artifact into its beam and it lifts the piece into the sky, spares you, and leaves. Every script check passed on its branch and again on staging. Pictures are on each item below; the Changes tab has short looping clips and a before-and-after of the beam.
short.hint: Tap an item to see what was checked and what you can try yourself.
items: It no longer floods your own view

On the target's own screen the beam fades out over its last 25 m and is 0.8 m wide at you, so you see the eye glow and your health drop, not a white wedge. Screenshot: docs/generated/ophan-418/staging-beam-host.png.

items.alt: The hunted player's own view while the slow beam drains them
items.caption: Your own view while being drained: the eye glows, health falls (90 here), and no white wedge covers the screen.

items: A new held pose in the sky
ophan_spread holds after the arrival: 13.2 m wide by 7.8 m tall on the model (the old hover was 11.7 by 9.5). Review sheet: docs/art/anim/fear/ophan_spread.png.

items.alt: The spread-wing pose turning on the review stage
items.caption: The new held pose, looping: wings spread wide, rings turning, eye drifting.

items: The host carried an artifact into the open: after the 3-second lock-on the piece was gone, the host stayed at 100 health, the Ophan left, and both machines showed the piece rising up the beam. Screenshot: staging-lift-host.png.

items.alt: A taken piece rising up toward the Ophan's eye
items.caption: The taken piece (the gold mask, left of the eye) on its way up into the sky.

items: Lock-on, then the drain; stepping behind stone stopped it and health held; after 3 s in cover the eye swelled and blazed, the charged beam killed through the stone, and both machines showed the room scorched black.

items.alt: The Ophan's eye swelling and blazing, then the charged beam firing
items.caption: The charge, from the other player's view: the eye swells and blazes, then the charged beam fires.

items: After a kill, the next player gets the lock-on
In co-op the Ophan used to drain the next player at once after a kill. Now any new target gets the full 3-second lock-on first. Covered by a new test and the co-op check.

items.alt: The other player's view as the Ophan locks on to them
items.caption: After the kill: the next player is locked on first (health still 100).

items: Staging: EditMode 274 passed / 3 skipped, PlayMode 529 of 529, the Ophan check 14 of 14, and the Wick, Lair (27 of 27) and raid-length (301.3 s) checks all passed. The feature branch matched, apart from one carry-feel timing test known to be flaky since September, which passed on a rerun.

items.alt: A castle room from above with its walls scorched black
items.caption: The scorched room from above: its walls are burnt black on both machines, so the slow beam now passes through it.

items: Set out with a friend and stay until the last minute. One of you picks up loot and stands in the open; then hide behind a wall for a few seconds; then try it carrying an artifact.
Tell me how the drone and shake feel, whether the beam reads from both views, and whether the lifted piece is easy to see.

wrapup.summary: The Ophan in the sky is built and passes every script check on its branch and on staging.
wrapup.changing: Every raid is hunted for now (a test switch on OphanOfHours) until the demand (#419) decides when.
wrapup.blocking: #418 stays open until your QA pass. Main is not touched; PR #437 still waits on your manual co-op test.
wrapup.next: After you pass it, #419 (the demand itself) branches off staging.
